correctness.rationale: The exact graph-distance categories, orthogonal symmetry decomposition and standard 2-by-2 block are verified algebraically. The block determinant has a unique root in (0,1), while all other zero-sum components remain strictly negative at that root: endpoint paired-antisymmetric eigenvalue -2^p, untouched-vertex eigenvalue -1, and global-mode matrix determinant 2r(1-c)k+(r/t)[6-2c+4(r-1)k]>0 for t>0 (or strictly negative explicit scalar form for t=0). The critical kernel has dimension r-1. Li–Weston gives lower-exponent strictness; the standard block yields failure at every higher exponent. Schoenberg rank gives embedding dimensions. Independently reconstructed BFS distances and complete projected spectra pass 136 recorded checks across 16 graphs; computation is not used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The exact universal p-negative-type endpoint, its r-1-dimensional critical kernel and endpoint affine dimension m for the once-subdivided matching family are absent from the inspected directly relevant primary theorems. The 2018 deleted-matching theorem concerns a different metric without inserted vertices; the 2020 and 2024 graph-join computations concern p=1 and graphs admitting nontrivial joins, whereas for r>=2 the present graph has a connected complement and distances of three between inserted vertices. The 2009 Li–Weston result is general interval theory. Query-based historical uniqueness is not asserted.

value.rationale: Once-subdividing a matching of a clique is a canonical minimal graph perturbation of the deleted-matching class. Despite arbitrary clique order and matching size >=2, the entire infinite family shares one nontrivial exponent strictly below 1, while its exact critical equality multiplicity increases with matching size. This is a complete, motivated Hilbert-snowflake embedding classification and a structural distinction between edge deletion and vertex-inserting subdivision, not merely a finite table or a numerical recomputation. The boundary r=1 is explicitly excluded.
